messages:
anya: Idea: for air-gapped upgrades let's staple a small "manifest-of-manifests" that contains final commit pins + per-node reprofiles. This would let verifier accept partial seeds and still validate final activation without waiting for full blob transfer.
ben: Wait1 how would "stapling" work in offline mode? Do you mean signing the manifest with a CA and bundling the signature?
anya: Exactly. The operator produces a signed head manifest (compact) with entries like: `(component, version, sha256, compressed_size, weight)` and a KMS-signed envelope. That head can be transferred first (tiny) so verifiers can pre-validate layout and reserve space.
claire: That helps for sizing and avoiding mid-apply OOMs. Also we can compute a per-node plan: which shards come from seed vs. delta.
dmitri: Concern: if head is signed once but we later generate deltas, signatures change. How do we ensure the activation epoch is immutable?
anya: We treat the head manifest as the activation anchor. Any subsequent delta must be signed and reference the anchor by digest. Agents reject applies that don't chain to the anchor. This gives cryptographic continuity.
ben: Nice. Also suggests a two-phase fetch: 1) transfer head, validators run offline checks; 2) transfer heavy blobs in staggered batches.
anya: Right. Staggered reseed: nodes self-schedule based on a global window and local profiling. Config example: `reseed: {window: 3h, batch_size: 4, max_parallel_bytes: 2e9, probe_rate: 128k}`
claire: We should also support an admin override: `manual_stitch=true` to allow techs to put blobs on local media and mark nodes as "staged".
dmitri: On-disk marker format suggestion: `/var/redwood/anchors/<epoch>.anchor` contains `anchor_digest`, `signed_by`, `staged_shards:[..]`, `applied_bytes`. Keep it newline-delimited JSON for easy tailing.
anya: Good. For rollback semantics: activation only flips to COMMITTED when controller sees >quorum committed markers. Otherwise after soft_timeout we enter HUNG and allow operator to issue abort.
ben: How to surface progress? We must translate applied_bytes -> ETA. Use per-node throughput baseline plus a conservative multiplier. Show both optimistic and conservative.
claire: UX: show "anchor accepted" -> "staging" -> "applying (n/m)" -> "verifying" -> "committed". Keep it minimal.
dmitri: Edge-case: powercut during final verify. Agents should write a `verifying` marker before heavy fsync step, and a `commit-intent` marker after verify success. On restart, controller inspects markers and either completes commit or runs deterministic rollback.
anya: We also need to avoid frequent controller churn affecting activation windows. Proposal: controller grants a soft lease for head acceptance and a separate apply lease for heavy fetch. Head lease TTL is short (minutes); apply lease has grace_soft and grace_hard.
ben: Can we reuse our existing epoch token system? Keep semantics but add `anchor_digest` binding. Controller allocates `apply_tokens` based on node group capacity.
anya: Yes. Also add a safety cap: `max_total_bandwidth_per_group` so a single upgrade can't saturate all nodes.
devex-bot: noted. I can wire a telemetry card for the UI: `anchor_digest`, `stage`, `applied_bytes`, `total_bytes`, `ETA_conservative`, `ETA_opt`. Will need agent to emit `progress` pings every 10s.
claire: For CI: we need a lightweight sim that can replay anchor chaining, slow filesystems, and partial-blob corruption. Use FUSE to emulate flaky IO.
dmitri: For security: signed anchors must be verifiable with customer KMS keys. We must support offline verification: include public key(s) in the head or a PKI path.
anya: Agree. Default operator flow: generate head anchor -> sign with operator key -> push to airgap media -> operator imports head -> controller validates -> controller issues apply tokens -> nodes fetch blobs -> nodes write markers -> controller finalizes commit.
ben: If a node fails mid-apply, others can continue. But commit requires quorum. If quorum fails, rollback plan: nodes revert to previous runtime snapshot using tombstone markers.
anya: We'll keep rollback idempotent by shipping a `rollback_plan` in the head with ordered revert steps.
dmitri: One more: retention. How long do we keep anchors/blobs for quick rollback? Maybe default 7 days; configurable.
anya: Good default. We'll add `retention_days`.
claire: Ok this is shaping into an RFC. I'll draft the operator UX and progress card.
ben: I'll write controller-token semantics and bandwidth caps.
dmitri: I'll author marker formats and restart state machine.
ops-bot: created rfc/airgap-stapled-anchors-389 by anya (draft). reviewers: ben, claire, dmitri.
anya: Thanks all. Short call tomorrow 9am PT to align on public key packaging and CI harness.
claire: 9am works for me.
ben: Works.
dmitri: Works.
anya: I'll open the PR with diagrams and a minimal config schema.
